notes.meaning: David resolves to thank and praise the Lord continually, through every circumstance in life. His gratitude is not hidden in his heart, but openly spoken aloud. God showed him mercy and rescued him even when he was in deep danger and made foolish mistakes.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars view the psalm as a later poem whose title was added by an editor using wordplays rather than being an eyewitness record of David's life.

notes.meaning: David brags not in his own cleverness, but entirely in the goodness and power of the Lord. When humble people who are beaten down by troubles hear how God saved him, their hearts will be lifted up with joy. Believers are encouraged when they hear how God helps others in distress.

David invites everyone to join him in declaring how great God is. God cannot literally be made bigger, but His honor and fame grow in our eyes when we worship Him. Praise is sweetest when God's people come together in united worship.

David prayed earnestly in his moment of terror, and God answered his plea. The Lord not only removed the danger, but also freed David's heart from fear itself. Even weak and imperfect prayers are heard when offered in true dependence on God.

Anyone who looks to God in trusting faith receives comfort and joy that brightens their whole face. They will never be left feeling ashamed or disappointed in their hope. Looking to the Lord brings light to the soul just as the sun brings light to the eyes.

David speaks of himself as a poor, helpless man who had no power of his own. He cried out to God in his distress, and the Lord heard him and brought him safely through every trial. God does not look down on the lowly, but welcomes their honest cries.

God places heavenly protection all around those who revere and obey Him. Just like an army camping around a king's tent, divine guards keep watch on every side to rescue believers from harm. Believers can rest peacefully knowing God's defenders are near.

differ.view: Some in this tradition view the angel as referring collectively to the entire host of God's ministering angels sent to guard His people.
Many Baptists understand the angel of the Lord to be the pre-incarnate Christ standing as Captain over heaven's armies to defend His saints.

notes.meaning: David urges others to test God's goodness for themselves through personal faith and experience. Just as honey must be tasted to know its sweetness, God's kindness must be experienced in the heart to be truly known. The person who puts their trust in Him discovers true, lasting happiness.

God's holy people are called to fear Him with loving, childlike reverence and honor His commands. Those who revere the Lord in this way will never lack what is truly necessary for life and godliness. True reverence for God frees a person from every other fear.

Even strong, fierce young lions sometimes go hungry when their hunting fails. In contrast, those who seek the Lord will never lack any genuinely good thing. God supplies all real needs, giving His people contentment and whatever is best for their spiritual growth.

David turns like a caring father or teacher to address those willing to learn, especially the young and teachable. He does not offer lessons in warfare or politics, but in the fear of the Lord, which is true religion. Learning to honor God early in life lays the only foundation for true blessing.

David asks who truly wants to enjoy a long, peaceful, and satisfying life. Everyone naturally desires happiness, but few look in the right place to find it. Real life is not just breathing for many years, but experiencing the goodness and favor of God.

The first step in living well is learning to control the words we speak. We must keep our tongues from speaking harmful things, lies, and deceit. A clean and honest tongue keeps the conscience clear and prevents misery.

Living for God requires running away from sin and actively doing good deeds to help others. Believers must also love peace and chase after it, even when peace seems hard to find or maintain. True goodness is not just avoiding harm, but doing positive good in the world.

The Lord watches over righteous people with tender care, never taking His eyes off them. He leans in close to hear their prayers, just like a loving parent listening for the cry of a sick child. Even a faint, broken prayer will reach His ears.

God sets His face against those who choose a lifestyle of evil and rebellion. Instead of finding lasting honor, evildoers will face destruction, and their very memory will fade from the earth. Lasting peace and honor come only from God's blessing, not from wickedness.

When godly people find themselves in deep trouble, they cry out to the Lord for help. God pays close attention to their cries and delivers them from all their hardships. Afflictions drive believers to prayer, and prayer brings God's rescue.

The Lord stays especially close to people whose hearts are broken and crushed under the weight of grief or sorrow for sin. Being contrite means being completely humbled, with our pride and self-confidence broken down like rock under a hammer. God does not abandon those who feel helpless, but brings them comfort and salvation.

God does not promise that good people will have an easy life free of suffering; in fact, the righteous often face many trials. Yet the Lord promises to bring them safely through every single hardship. Troubles may hurt believers for a season, but God will not let those troubles destroy them.

God guards the essential framework of the righteous person, protecting them from total ruin. While a good person may suffer physical injuries, their life and soul remain secure under God's watchful care. This promise also pointed forward to Jesus on the cross, whose legs were not broken by the soldiers.

Evil carries its own punishment and will ultimately destroy those who love it. Those who hate God's people will face condemnation and be left desolate and abandoned. Wicked deeds inevitably turn back upon the head of the sinner.

The Lord purchases and rescues the lives of His faithful servants, saving them from spiritual ruin. No one who runs to God for safety will ever be condemned or forsaken. Those who trust in Him are held safe forever in His mercy.
